claim: Traffic signals adapt through distributed consensus with neighboring intersections, creating coordinated green waves
mechanism: Each intersection communicates its current state and planned adjustments to adjacent intersections, then reaches consensus on timing that balances local and network-wide objectives
evidence: Distributed consensus algorithms work in other network systems
Coordinated signal systems exist but typically require central planning
assumptions: Intersections can communicate with immediate neighbors
Network-wide objectives can be approximated through local interactions
expected_failure_modes: Inability to reach consensus during rapidly changing conditions
novelty_rationale: Transfers the myxomycete network adaptation principle through distributed consensus rather than purely local decision-making
testability: Can be tested by implementing communication between adjacent intersections and measuring convergence time and solution quality
falsifier: If the communication overhead required for consensus makes real-time adaptation infeasible or if consensus cannot be reached quickly enough to respond to changing conditions
